text:
eli: quick note after the RFC review 1 we still haven't settled the sidecar -> ingest ownership model. two broad paths: 1) full attribution at edge (sidecar writes final attribution) or 2) lightweight fingerprint + async enrichment in ingest.
maria: i'm leaning toward doing as much as possible in the sidecar for auditability, but worried about CPU/latency on high-throughput hosts. also shard hotness if we hash on tenant id.
eli: agreed. sidecar-first gives immediate correctness and simpler audits; downside is heavier sidecars and tighter coupling to attribution logic.
sam: alternative: sidecar emits a compact fingerprint + provenance headers and a flag if attribution is "uncertain". ingest routes uncertain events to an enrichment pool that claims work by fingerprint. reduces edge load but complicates reconciliation.
nina: duplicate credits are manageable with ledger idempotency, but audit joins need both original fingerprint and final attribution so we can replay how a charge was decided. otherwise audits are painful.
eli: a hybrid could be best: sidecar performs a fast heuristic check (prefix match, small LRU cache, TTL lookup) and only marks events "need_enrich" if heuristic confidence is low. Most events remain cheap and fully attributed.
maria: how do we compute confidence? maybe a simple rule-set: exact KV hit -> confident, low token count -> confident, otherwise fallback. keep it deterministic and explainable.
sam: implement routing like: {fingerprint, provenance, need_enrich:bool}. Router: if need_enrich true -> route to enrichment pool with affinity to fingerprint (consistent hashing) + leaser to avoid duplicate workers. add exponential backoff on retries.
eli: enrichment worker writes final attribution record referencing original fingerprint and emits ledger entry that points to both fingerprint and enrichment_id. audit view can join on either.
nina: we must define an enrichment TTL (e.g., 6h). if enrichment doesn't complete in TTL, apply fallback attribution policy (last-known owner or "unattributed") and mark for later cleanup. avoid indefinite pending credits.
maria: ops question: tenant shard-key migration. if we change hashing or shard function, enrichment workers need to accept both old and new fingerprint variants for a grace period. plan: dual-hash acceptance + replay window.
sam: lease protocol sketch: worker claims fingerprint for N seconds, streams enrichment progress to a checkpoint, if claim expired another worker can pick up using op-log. workers must write idempotency keys to ledger to avoid double-credits.
eli: metrics to add: sidecar heuristic hit rate, percent of events flagged need_enrich, enrichment queue depth, enrichment latencies (p50/p95), reconciliation resolved ratio. also an ops alarm for enrichment backlog growth.
maria: rollout plan: 1) feature-flagged sidecar heuristic 2) add need_enrich header in router 3) enrichment pool + lease logic 4) ledger write that stores both fingerprint and enrichment_id 5) audit join views and TTL fallback.
nina: canary: pick two tenants (one noisy, one normal) to observe hot-shard behavior and eviction patterns. if we see affinity hotspots, add tenant burst shaping and probabilistic sampling for enrichment.
eli: perf target: sidecar extra work should be <5ms p50. router and enrichment path SLOs TBD but enrichment backlog should stay < 5 minutes for 99% after canary.
sam: i'll stub the enrichment worker and lease proto in the spike. include a small local harness to simulate tenant bursts.
maria: i'll add the audit queries and define the TTL/fallback policy doc.
nina: i'll write the runbook: what to do if enrichment backlog grows, how to force re-enrichment for a tenant, and migration steps when shard hashing changes.
metering-bot: reminder: RFC follow-up meeting tomorrow 16:00 UTC. agenda: checklist + canary schedule + perf targets.
eli: thanks all. i'll open a draft PR with the sidecar heuristic and test vectors. will ping channel when ready.
